(1) MKL using nonverbal features outperformed traditional machine learning techniques, (2) MKL and a proposed simple heuristic can be used together to find the best performing nonverbal features, and (3) significantly high correlation exists between the extracted nonverbals and social psychology questionnaire results
MKL is a powerful technique to predict the leadership style of a group and that speaking activity based and some of prosodic features are the best performing ones.

(1) MKL is able to predict the leadership style of emergent leaders in a more accurate way than traditional learning algorithms, (2) the best performing features can be selected with a simple heuristic proposed and (3) the nonverbal features that are significantly correlated with the leadership styles are the speaking activity based and the prosodic ones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction of leadership styles using nonverbal features in a dataset in the Wild.
the prediction of the leadership style of emergent leaders using nonverbal audio-visual data.
the prediction of an emergent leaders style and the identification of the most important features that contribute to the prediction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed MKL method is able to predict the leadership style of emergent leaders in the wild with an accuracy of 80%.
MKL is a promising method for the prediction of the leadership style of a leader in a group.

MKL can be used as an effective tool in predicting leadership styles using multimodal non-verbal features and that speaking activity and prosody are the best features for predicting leadership styles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MKL is a very promising tool for social signal processing and it should be used more often in the future.
MKL is very useful for the prediction of the leadership style and the nonverbal features that are extracted are highly correlated with the results of the social psychology questionnaire.

the leadership style of the leader can be successfully predicted using nonverbal features from audio and video modalities and that MKL is a promising technique to be used for multimodal data analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MKL is a promising tool to be used for the prediction of leadership style in an emergent leader.
the leadership style of a leader can be identified in a more effective way by utilizing MKL and nonverbal features extracted from multimodal data.
the proposed method and especially the MKL can be used for the prediction of the leadership style in a group of people and can be used in a more general setting for predicting other social phenomena.
